body:
Refresh: `origin/main` (`c41460870`) is merged into the branch. The new head is `e345c7145`. There was no rebase and no force-push.

Conflict files:

- `examples/first-router-part.camproj`: the only file with a conflict. Main saved the demo again (tab fix), and this branch changed the Drill1 feeds. Resolution:
  1. I took the side of main.
  2. I saved the demo again from its command build (`WRITE_GOLDEN=1`, test `first_router_part`).
  3. I compared the result with main. Only these lines are different:
     - the Drill1 `feed` and `plunge_feed` (150 -> 115);
     - the 16 cached drill moves (`"feed"` 150 -> 115);
     - the stamps of Drill1, 2D Pocket1 and 2D Contour1;
     - `"version"` 71 -> 72.
  4. The pocket and contour stamps read the drill. A test with only the drill lines changed in the file of main reported "2D Pocket1: inputs moved since generation". The new stamps are therefore necessary.
  5. Version 72 is the current `PROJECT_VERSION` on main (`7dce83aaf`).
- `examples/first-router-part.nc` and `examples/first-part.nc` merged without a conflict. I posted them again with the merged `camcraft-cli`. Against main, only the drill F words change (F150 -> F115 and F300 -> F115).

No source file had a conflict. No test of this branch builds finishing parameters by hand, so the new `gap_link` field needs no change here.

Tests on the new head:

- `hole_feed_rating`, `example_catalog`, `first_part_programs`, `first_router_part` and `continuous_4axis_part` pass.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main`: 568 steps, 0 failed.

<!-- pr-reviewer: e345c714557a071364a49c3522e2b13f3d062a8b -->
Review of #2668, head e345c7145. Built in a worktree: the head merged with current main (clean), then the touched suites and clippy ran.

Result: pass. No blockers.

What was run:
- `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test hole_feed_rating --test tool_cutting_rows --test first_router_part --test wcs_rotation_control --test lathe_workholding_kinds --test setup_align_hole_kinds --test stock_source_holes` - 7 binaries, 47 tests, all pass (1 ignored as on main).
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` - clean.

What the review checked:
- `feed_rating.rs`: the rating is the tool's row in force for the material, else `tool.feed`; `None` when not finite and positive, so no seed and no judgement. `judged_feed` reads the generated path's non-rapid feeds for a Drill (a tap cycle is not judged - its feed is rpm x pitch), and `feed.max(plunge_feed)` for a Thread. The clause sits in `verification_report`, so it blocks the post with the other blocking problems.
- The seeds run in one undo step at the quick-add (`seed_feed_for_tool`) and at a tool retarget (`retargeted_params` in `EditOperationLinks`); undo restores the old feeds (pinned). Explicit params, saved files and retypes keep their numbers; a project with a high feed loads unchanged and is refused at the post by name (pinned, save/open round trip).
- Golden diffs read as claimed: `first-router-part.camproj` changes only the Drill1 feeds 150 -> 115, the 16 cached drill moves, the 3 stamps (Drill1 and the two ops that read the drill), and `version` 71 -> 72; `first-router-part.nc` changes only the one G73 line F150 -> F115. No `.camproj` hand edits beyond these.
- A feed that equals the rating posts (SLACK 1e-6 on the compare); raising the tool's feed clears the refusal.

P1 floor: second review needed. This changes posted G-code (the hole cycles of the example programs) and adds a blocking post clause. The author's quick gate is green (568 steps) and this review is green; a read-only second review on the Opus model is required before the merge.

Second review (Opus, read-only, not built) of head e345c714557a071364a49c3522e2b13f3d062a8b.

Verdict: CLEAN. I found no blocker.

What I read: the diff against the merge base `c41460870`, `crates/motion/src/drilling/cycle.rs`, `crates/app/src/posting.rs` (the gate and its callers), `crates/app/src/mcp/edit.rs` (`add_operation`), `crates/app/src/cutting_rows.rs`, and the remerge-diff of the merge commit `e345c7145`. I did not build and I did not run a test.

Findings:

1. The P1 is closed for each Drill cycle. `feed_rating::problems` (`crates/app/src/operation/feed_rating.rs:104-133`) reads the feeds of the cached path. Spot, Drill, Peck (G73), Deep (G83), Bore, BackBore and Ream all put `plunge_feed` or `feed` on their non-rapid moves (`cycle.rs:129-183`), so the clause sees each posted cycle feed. The cross-hole frame (`cross.rs`) also writes its feeds on the path.
2. The clause is in `verification_report_by` (`posting.rs:969-970`). The single-file post, the per-mount post (`posting_mounts.rs:304-306`), the per-operation post (`posting_per_op.rs:204`) and the script API (`script/api.rs:262`) all call it. Thus each post dialect is gated. The refusal is visible and names the operation, the feed, the tool and the rating. The value of the user does not change: there is no silent clamp.
3. `program_ops` refuses an operation that is not generated or not fresh. Thus the clause always reads a current cached path when the post can continue. The `None` from a missing path or from an unreadable list cannot release a post.
4. Tapping: `judged_feed` (`feed_rating.rs:73-77`) uses the same test as the generator (`cycle.rs:33-35`). A Tap or FloatingTap cycle, or Auto with a Tap tool, is not judged. Its feed is `rpm x pitch`, and the clause does not refuse that synchronised feed. The Thread op (thread milling) is not synchronised, and the clause judges its stated edge feed and plunge feed. That is correct, because the posted arcs are scaled to the tool centre and are lower.
5. Units: the tool feed, the row feed and the path feeds are all mm/min inside the program. `units::feed` changes only the text of the message for an inch document. The compare does not depend on the program unit.
6. Plunge feed: a Drill seeds `feed` and `plunge_feed` to the rating. A Thread seeds the edge feed and holds `plunge_feed` at or below the rating. The clause judges the higher of the two for a Thread and each path feed for a Drill.
7. Pinning tests (`crates/app/tests/hole_feed_rating.rs`): each of the three tests fails without the fix. Before the fix the seed is 1200 / 300, so the `(115.0, 115.0)` asserts fail, `verify` returns `ok: true`, and `set_tool` does not move the feeds. The first test reads the posted F words of the G73/G81/G83 lines (F115) and checks that no F word is above 400.
8. Goldens: against the merge base, `examples/first-part.nc` and `examples/catalog/2d/first-part/first-part.nc` change only the four drill cycle F words (F300 -> F115). `examples/first-router-part.nc` changes only the G73 F word (F150 -> F115). `examples/first-router-part.camproj` changes only the Drill1 `feed` and `plunge_feed`, the 16 cached drill move feeds, the three stamps and `version` 71 -> 72. The remerge-diff of `e345c7145` agrees with the merge note. 115 is the feed of DR-0600 (`examples/first-part.camproj`, the DR-0600 tool entry, `"feed": 115.0`).
9. AGENTS.md: no `unwrap`, `expect` or `panic!` in new non-test code. `feed_rating.rs` has 133 lines. No new crate dependency, no snapshot PNG, no process file. The new test is in `crates/app/tests/` and imports `camcraft_app::mcp`. The decision entry `docs/decisions/2598-hole-op-tool-feed.md` is present. `posting.rs` was already above 400 lines on main; this PR adds 2 lines.

Follow-ups (not blockers):

- A. The rating is the cutting-data row that names the material in force, else the running feed (`feed_rating.rs:41-44`). `cutting_rows::follow_running` does not move a named row when the user edits the running feed. Thus, if the user lowers the running feed of a tool below its named row, an op at the row feed posts with no refusal. Recommend: judge against the lower of the running feed and the row, or say why not in the decision. Proposed priority: P3.
- B. A tool with a feed of zero or a feed that is not finite gives no rating (`rated_feed` returns `None`). Its Drill or Thread op is not judged, and nothing says so. Recommend: a not-judged line, as the sim clause gives. Proposed priority: P7.
- C. `examples/catalog/2d/first-part/first-part.camproj` was written at `version` 71, but `PROJECT_VERSION` is 72. The file also gets two fields from other work (`notes` on 2D Pocket1 and the tool `number` fields). The catalog test compares only the `.nc`, so this does not fail. Recommend: save the file again from `build.camscript` on the current main. Proposed priority: P7.
- D. The helical Bore op (`OpParams::Bore`) and the Circular op are hole operations with the 1200 / 300 seed, and the clause does not judge them. The decision puts milling kinds out of scope. Recommend: one issue to decide this. Proposed priority: P7.
- E. No test posts in an inch program, and no test covers the tap exclusion or a Drill with a cutting-data row for the material. Proposed priority: P7.
- F. An edit to a feed above the rating is accepted without a word, and the refusal comes only at the post. An advisory line in the `edit_operation` answer (as `clearance_warning` does) would tell the user earlier. Proposed priority: P7.

Compared with the first review (the PR-reviewer comment on this head): we agree on the result. Follow-ups A to F are not in that review.

Merge class: SAME. The reviewed head is the merged head, `e345c714557a071364a49c3522e2b13f3d062a8b`. No commit came after it.

This merge relies on two reviews of that head:
- the built review by SlaveSession (comment 7001810187), result pass;
- the read-only Opus second review (comment 7001940941), verdict CLEAN. The second review is necessary because the PR fixes a P1 (#2598).

The follow-ups A to F of the second review go into new issues.
